sources.note: Phonology section gives 13 consonants, 5 vowels and phonotactics; only prosodic remark: 'Central vowel [ə] is very common in Walker's vocabularies. It appears to be a destressed allophone of low central /a/.' Pronoun table reproduces Walker's stress-marked forms (Gaka ˈnodə, ˈorodə, ˈnada, jaˈrodə; Tairi ˈnoːdaʔ, jaˈɾoda, oˈroːda, ˈnaːdaʔ, ˈweːda). No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Walker, Roland W. & Ronald Hesse. 1988. Buruwai Wordlist in Tairi Village [UNCEN-SIL 3/85 'Daftar kata-kata, Propinsi Irian Jaya' form; Bahasa 'Madebana (Buruwai) - call themselves / Sebakor - Kamberau call them'; kampung Tairi, desa Buruwai, kec. sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The fullest primary Buruwai list (209 items), every form with an acute stress mark on one vowel (yebida, sarawera, duara, ubara, kebara, amunira.; numerals madabata, manabomara). The 'Notes on phonetics and transcription' box (p.5) contains a single symbol gloss, 'p-bar = vl. bilab. fric.', and nothing on stress, length or pitch; the grammar-notes page (p.6) has about eight elicited sentences (anak makan pisang = debura? oida? naparara [SOV]; saya memberi ikan kepada anak = noda debura aramura.; dua anjing = ibuda abomara; tense: noda samaruga / noida ana samarura / noida wabune samadagura) b…

sources.citation: Walker, Roland W. 1988. Buruwai Wordlist in Yarona Village [UNCEN-SIL form 3/85 'Daftar kata-kata, Propinsi Irian Jaya'; bahasa 'Sebakor (Bhs. Gunung)', desa Buruwai, kampung Yarona, speaker Amos Kawada 55; 127-item list + supplementary vocabulary + sociolinguistic questionnaire; dated 20 Jan 1988]. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 57793, 7 pp. (= Glottolog hh:578419 'Walker 1988 Sebakor').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content: handwritten phonetic transcriptions carry an acute accent (stress mark) on one vowel of most words (e.g. yebida 'kepala', pida 'rambut', bidapura 'mulut', sarawera 'danau', apera 'angin', wanamara 'langit' with accent marks); the form's box 'Notes on phonetics and transcription' is left blank and the 'Grammar notes' page (word order, tense, person) is blank; p.6 has only livelihood/religion/language-use notes (children do not speak the vernacular well; adults used Indonesian with the surveyor). Stress marks on individual items = wordlist-only data, no statement of stress…

sources.note: Sec. 2.6.2.2.6.1.1 'Iria and Asienara', pp.369-370: phoneme inventory (p t k b d g m n s h/f r w y; i e a o u (ə)) 'as far as it could be ascertained from the wordlists' + pronouns; 'Language materials are restricted to the lexical data in Anceaux' lists'; 'Further grammatical information is at present not available.' Silent on stress (whereas for Kamoro on the same page he notes Drabbe marks stress but gives no rules).
